Does your restaurant need a menu site or an ordering site?

Choose between a simple menu, WhatsApp ordering, and an online checkout based on how your team handles orders.

Webly · 9 November 2026 · Buyer guide · 1 min read

Start with a menu if customers mainly need information

A simple mobile menu can answer the common questions about dishes, portions, opening hours, and how to contact you. It suits businesses that change the menu regularly or confirm orders by phone. Put the useful details in page text so customers can read them without zooming into a PDF.

Add a basket when orders need several choices

A basket helps when one order might include multiple dishes, quantities, or portion sizes. With WhatsApp ordering, the site passes those choices into a message. Your team still handles availability, fulfilment, and payment in the conversation. Plan how you will respond during your busiest hours.

Scope a checkout when you need to take payment online

An online checkout also needs decisions about stock, delivery areas, fees, payment confirmation, cancellations, and refunds. Write down who will manage each part before commissioning the build. If customers regularly ask how to pay online or your team spends time re-entering orders, a checkout or order dashboard may be the next useful step.
